sentences.text: This dinosaur measured approximately 8 to 9 meters in length.
Its name, Chebsaurus, translates to "young man" in colloquial Arabic, reflecting the initial belief that the fossils belonged to a juvenile.
Researchers originally nicknamed this animal "the Giant of Ksour" upon its description.
A second juvenile skeleton from the same region is also known to science.
Skeletal remains were uncovered in the Ksour Mountains within the Occidental Saharan Atlas.
The species Chebsaurus algeriensis was formally named in 2005 by Mahammed and colleagues.
Chebsaurus algeriensis serves as the type species for the genus.
It is a member of the family Cetiosauridae.
Taxonomically, the animal falls within the class Saurischia.
This creature inhabited present-day Algeria during the Callovian stage of the Jurassic period.
Its existence spanned between 165.3 and 161.5 million years ago.
